ai.description: The Banded Krait reaches 1.5–2 meters. It features alternating broad black and yellow rings with a prominent vertebral ridge, giving the body a distinct triangular cross-section.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Bungarus fasciatus* is uniquely identified by its prominent, triangular-shaped cross-section and a distinct vertebral ridge that runs along the length of its body.
ai.habitat: The Banded Krait inhabits open plains, agricultural lands, and tropical forests, typically near water sources at elevations below 1,500 meters across the Indian subcontinent.
ai.behavior: The banded krait is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a shy, docile temperament, often hiding its head under its coils when threatened rather than striking.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Banded Krait is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–14 eggs in underground retreats. Breeding typically occurs during the warmer months, often peaking around April–May.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Banded Krait occurs across Northeast India, West Bengal, and Odisha, ranging from sea level up to 1,500 meters in the Himalayan foothills and Indo-Burmese forests.
